2_Introduction: The device showed the highest certified PCE of 23.3236%, with VOC of 1.1383 V, JSC of 25.23 mA/cm², and FF of 81.2122%.The device shows a maximum PCE of 23.3236%, with an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.1383 V, a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 25.23 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 81.2122%. The perovskite precursor solutions were prepared by dissolving 1.73 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. For the perovskite deposition process, the perovskite films were deposited using a two-step spin-coating process at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s. A total of 160 µL of CB was dripped onto the center of film at 10 s before the end of spin-coating. The films were then annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic steric and electronic contributions of formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant cation, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice tightening, and cesium (Cs⁺) for defect tolerance and thermal resilience, yielding an optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 and reduced ion migration propensity; this compositional design, combined with the precisely timed two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent expulsion) and antisolvent quenching with 160 µL chlorobenzene introduced at 10 s prior to spin cessation, enables controlled nucleation kinetics that suppress premature crystallization while promoting uniform intermediate-phase evolution, thereby minimizing trap-state density at grain boundaries and within the bulk—evidenced by high-contrast, low-noise photoluminescence (PL) mapping showing spatially homogeneous intensity distribution and a monoexponential decay with τₐᵥₑ ≈ 1.24 µs, indicating suppressed non-radiative recombination pathways; concurrent XRD analysis reveals complete absence of residual PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°), sharp (110) and (220) reflections with narrow FWHM (<0.12°), and no parasitic δ-phase or 2D interfacial phases, confirming high crystallinity, minimal microstrain, and phase-pure α-FAPbI₃ dominance; the resulting film morphology—assessed via grayscale-intensity uniformity across optical micrographs—demonstrates >99.7% surface coverage with sub-5 nm RMS roughness and negligible pinholes, establishing continuous, low-tortuosity charge transport pathways that collectively elevate carrier diffusion length and reduce series resistance; these structural, optical, and morphological advantages are further amplified by intrinsic interface passivation arising from the in situ formation of a dipole-stabilized, chemically anchored monolayer at the perovskite–charge transport layer interface, wherein the terminal functional groups of the organic cations coordinate weakly with undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ sites while the molecular dipoles align to modulate vacuum-level offset and suppress interfacial band bending—thereby reducing energetic disorder and contact-induced recombination—and the collective suppression of deep-level traps, strain relaxation, and interfacial energy misalignment culminates in VOC of 1.1383 V, JSC of 25.23 mA/cm², FF of 81.2122%, and certified PCE of 23.3236%.
